title: Cross-Validation and Data Splitting Protocols
description: Validation schemes to ensure unbiased model performance estimation without data leakage.
conditions: Training and evaluating any supervised machine learning model
Dataset exhibits class imbalance, grouping structure (e.g. repeated measures per patient), or temporal ordering
recommended_methods: Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation (typically 5 or 10 folds) for imbalanced classification
GroupKFold to ensure all records for a given entity (e.g. Patient ID) remain exclusively in train or test fold
TimeSeriesSplit (expanding or rolling window) for chronologically ordered observations
selection_rules: If data has a temporal timestamp index, NEVER use standard random K-Fold; use TimeSeriesSplit to prevent look-ahead bias
If multiple records belong to the same entity/customer, always use GroupKFold on entity ID
Execute all feature scaling, imputation, and encoding strictly INSIDE each cross-validation fold
limitations: Standard K-Fold drastically underestimates generalization error when applied to autocorrelated time-series
Cross-validation increases training wall-clock compute time by a factor of K
